content: 1. The methodology was validated by the Guideline Development Group (GDG) members and includes a series of steps that clinicians must follow when accessing a peripheral intravenous catheter (PIVC). 2. Before starting the procedure, clean the workspace where the PIVC pack and materials will be placed. Use an appropriate disinfectant to wipe the area, and then gather all necessary materials. 3. Perform proper hand hygiene before touching the patient, as per the first moment of hand hygiene. 4. Position the patient to allow optimal visualization of the PIVC access site and ensure their comfort. Inspect the PIVC access site for any abnormalities. 5. Perform hand hygiene again, as per the fourth and second moments of hand hygiene. 6. Open the sterile pack(s) containing the required materials for PIVC access. Ensure all contents are easily accessible while avoiding contact with the internal sterile surfaces of the pack. Pour the disinfectant solution (e.g., 2% chlorhexidine gluconate with 70% alcohol) into the sterile container provided in the pack. If using a pre-soaked swab, open the swab packet and drop it onto the sterile zone without touching the swab. 7. Perform hand hygiene before proceeding with the aseptic technique or procedure, as per the second moment of hand hygiene. 8. If gloves are used, put on single-use gloves, ensuring not to touch potentially contaminated surfaces such as the outside of the glove box or nearby areas. 9. Thoroughly clean the intended PIVC access site using a hub disinfectant solution and allow it to dry completely. 10. Carefully draw up the intravenous (IV) product intended for administration into a sterile syringe. If flushing is required, prepare a second syringe with sterile saline. Place the syringes on the sterile field, away from other items. 11. For an open PIVC hub access system: Remove the PIVC access cap and place it on the sterile field, away from other items. Promptly connect the loaded syringe to the open PIVC hub device, avoiding air entry and ensuring no contact between the PIVC hub, syringe tip, and fingers. Slightly aspirate the syringe to withdraw any accessed air and confirm blood return, indicating PIVC patency. Administer the required IV product. If necessary, flush the PIVC with a compatible sterile fluid (e.g., saline). Remove the syringe and promptly replace the PIVC access cap without touching other items. 12. For a closed PIVC hub access system: Thoroughly clean the PIVC access hub with a disinfectant solution and allow it to dry. Attach a needleless administration device to the loaded syringe and insert it into the closed access hub device, following the manufacturer’s instructions. Slightly aspirate the syringe to confirm blood return, indicating PIVC patency. Administer the required IV product. If necessary, flush the PIVC with a compatible sterile fluid (e.g., saline). Remove the syringe and needleless device, then clean the PIVC access hub with a disinfectant solution and allow it to dry. 13. Dispose of all syringes, needles, and other used materials in an appropriate waste disposal system, including a sharps container if applicable. Ensure waste containers are within arm’s reach during the procedure. 14. Wipe the working area and any trays used with an appropriate disinfectant. 15. Remove gloves and perform hand hygiene after completing the aseptic procedure and after touching the patient, as per the third and fourth moments of hand hygiene. 16. For PIVC maintenance and dressing changes, follow similar steps, ensuring the workspace is cleaned and disinfected before starting. Gather all necessary materials and perform hand hygiene before touching the patient. 17. Position the patient for optimal visualization of the PIVC site and ensure their comfort. Perform hand hygiene again before proceeding. 18. Open the sterile pack(s) containing the required components for PIVC maintenance and dressing change. Avoid touching the internal sterile surfaces of the pack. Pour the disinfectant solution into the sterile container or prepare a pre-soaked swab as needed. 19. Carefully remove the old PIVC dressing and dispose of it immediately in an appropriate waste container. If gloves become contaminated during dressing removal, replace them with a new pair before handling the new dressing. 20. Clean the skin around the PIVC insertion site and dressing area thoroughly with a disinfectant solution. Allow the area to dry completely. 21. Apply the new PIVC dressing over the insertion site and base, ensuring only the outer edges of the dressing are touched to avoid contamination. Secure the dressing to the skin without causing traction. 22. Dispose of all used materials in an appropriate waste disposal system. Wipe the workspace with a disinfectant, remove gloves, and perform hand hygiene. 23. Aseptic no-touch techniques are critical for PIVC maintenance and dressing changes to prevent bloodstream infections and other healthcare-associated infections. 24. Clinicians must adhere to evidence-based practices, such as care bundles, to improve patient outcomes. These bundles consist of structured interventions that, when performed collectively and reliably, yield better results than individual actions. 25. Hand hygiene is a fundamental practice in infection prevention, encompassing actions like antiseptic hand rubbing or washing with soap and water. Proper hand hygiene reduces the risk of healthcare-associated infections, which are among the most frequent adverse events in patient care. 26. Multimodal improvement strategies (MMIS) are essential for implementing interventions effectively. These strategies include system changes, training, monitoring, reminders, and fostering a culture of safety, all tailored to the local healthcare context.
